newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Suez CEO invites Belgian Frere to up stake to 7pct.
newsitem.headline: Suez CEO invites Belgian Frere to up stake to 7pct.

text.p: Gerard Mestrallet, chief executive officer of French Compagnie de Suez, has invited Belgian financier Albert Frere to boost his share stake in Suez to seven percent on Thursday.

"Albert Frere does not have to stop when he reaches five percent. He can go to seven percent. But that is the limit. I will never accept a dominant shareholder in Suez," Mestrallet was quoted as saying in Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd on Thursday.
Frere heads Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL).

A GBL unit bought a 2.9 percent stake in Suez from Elf Aquitaine on October 7 and was reported by French financial daily newspaper L'Agefi on October 23 to have taken another one percent from French insurer UAP.
Since then GBL is said to have boosted its stake to five percent. Frere is seeking a seat on Suez' board.

"Albert Frere has not informed us that he has reached the five percent threshold. And there is no request for a mandate. But I repeat that Frere is welcome." Seven percent was "the ideal stake" in Suez, Mestrallet said, referring to stakes held by French Saint Gobain and UAP.
"Suez has a tradition of stable minority shareholders. A Suez shareholder with a 10 percent stake would be a new fact," he said.
Suez shareholder UAP is a longtime ally of the reclusive financier Frere. UAP and GBL together control Belgian insurer Royale Belge SA.
